name: Find The Array
description: You are given an array $$$[a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n]$$$ such that $$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$. Let $$$S$$$ be the sum of all elements of the array $$$a$$$. Let's call an array $$$b$$$ of $$$n$$$ integers beautiful if: $$$1 \le b_i \le 10^9$$$ for each $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$; for every pair of adjacent integers from the array $$$(b_i, b_{i + 1})$$$, either $$$b_i$$$ divides $$$b_{i + 1}$$$, or $$$b_{i + 1}$$$ divides $$$b_i$$$ (or both); $$$2 \sum \limits_{i = 1}^{n} |a_i - b_i| \le S$$$. Your task is to find any beautiful array. It can be shown that at least one beautiful array always exists.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. Each test case consists of two lines. The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, print the beautiful array $$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$$$ ($$$1 \le b_i \le 10^9$$$) on a separate line. It can be shown that at least one beautiful array exists under these circumstances. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
approach_summary: Apply Bitwise Operations and Bitmasks paradigm under the Basics framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
